newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS- New barrage of supply hits mkt.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS- New barrage of supply hits mkt.

text.p: The corporate bond market was hit with another barrage of new debt offerings as $2.3 billion in new public debt, coupled with $2.1 billion in private placements, hit the market, players said.
"There's a good tone to the market ... everything you look at, the interest rate environment, the spread environment -- the market's in good shape," a high-grade syndicate source said.
Falling interest rates continue to lure U.S. corporations in search of cheaper financing into the debt arena.
Philip Morris issued a $1.0 billion eight-year global issue at 79 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch.
The issue traded a basis point tighter when freed, players said.

Merrill Lynch also underwrote Norwest Financial's $500 million two-part debt offering, which included $250 million in seven-year debt at 38 basis points over Treasuries and $250 million in 12-year debt at 60 basis points.
Waste Management sold $300 million in five-year notes at 50 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch, as well.
Pohang Iron & Steel sold $200 million in seven-year debt at 92 basis points via JP Morgan Securities.
Another $1.65 billion in debt came via the 144A private placement market, dealers said.
In the secondary trading arena, RJR Nabisco's 10-year paper was quoted at 205 bid, 200 offer.

Among the issues, was Safeco Corp's $850 million in 144A 40-year capital securities which priced at a spread of 148 basis points. Its other $200 million 10-year 144A tranche was priced at 69 basis points over, sources said.
Another $600 million in 10-year 144A notes came from HMH Properties, sources added.

In the secondary arena, Niagara Mohawk bonds tightened on news that it and 16 Independent Power Producers (IPP) had signed a master restructuring agreement to terminate or restructure 29 IPP contracts, representing more than 80 percent of Niagara's above-market IPP costs.
"Niagara Mohawk bonds have tightened at least 10 basis points, in some cases better than that," said one utility trader.
Niagara's 6-5/8 percent paper due 2005 was quoted 10 basis points tighter at 128 bid, 120 offer. Its 8.0 percent bonds due 2004 tightened 14 basis points, traders said.
The transaction is expected to reduce electricity prices for Niagara customers and help expedite competition.
After the news, Standard & Poor's said it was keeping Niagara Mohawk's credit ratings under review for a possible upgrade.

The rating agency said it was reviewing the agreement and would meet with Niagara Mohawk's management in the immediate future prior to determining the appropriateness of raising the corporate credit, senior secured, senior unsecured and preferred stock ratings.
S&P is considering a move higher within "distinctive speculative" category, which spans from B-minus to BB-plus.
S&P currently rates the electric and gas utility's senior secured debt at BB-minus, its senior unsecured debt at single-B and the firm's preferred stock at B-minus.
In other news, Grand Union 12 percent bonds continued to weaken, falling another 1-1/2 points to 66-3/4 bid, after a 1-3/4 drop on Wednesday, players said.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
